payload.title: judge-executor.mjs's judgeDiscovery/judgeDecompose dispatch (used by fgos discover/decompose, the
payload.description: judge-executor.mjs's judgeDiscovery/judgeDecompose dispatch (used by fgos discover/decompose, the highest-frequency headless judge call in the whole system) never uses capacity-aware dispatch -- judge-executor.mjs:154,297 calls resolveExecutorCommand(cfg, {prompt, model, tier}) with no capacityId, always hardcoded tier:'judge' (always Claude). tsk-62v's capacities mechanism (capacityId > tier > global precedence) already exists and has one proven consumer (tsk-5l2's submit-assist-classify) -- wiring judgeDiscovery/judgeDecompose through capacityId ('judge-discovery'/'judge-decompose') would let an operator route this frequent, structured judgment call to a cheaper backend, the exact cost objective tsk-64p's whole cluster was built for, currently unrealized for the system's own core loop. Small, config+wiring scope, no new mechanism needed. Depends on tsk-32n (capacities.<id>.allowCrossProvider governance, since routing judge to a non-Claude backend would need it) if a non-Claude backend is ever actually configured for it. Design record: docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md, plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260731-1758-capacity-backend-dispatch-proposal-report.md.

payload.title: Domain-2 (in-session Agent/Task tool dispatch) capacity-aware routing is a known, unclaimed design
payload.description: Domain-2 (in-session Agent/Task tool dispatch) capacity-aware routing is a known, unclaimed design gap in the agent-executor cluster. tsk-5l2's own scope explicitly deferred it (point 9: 'domain-2 is a separate item, deliberately out of scope here'), and no backlog item exists for it yet (checked). Today, every in-session subagent spawn (Explore, code-reviewer, cavecrew-*, etc, via the Agent/Task tool) always runs full Claude, unconditionally -- unlike domain-1 (headless runner), which already routes through capacities.<id> via tsk-62v's mechanism. Applying the same 'cheapest cost for adequate quality' objective to domain-2 would let a skill declare a capacityId for a specific subagent task (e.g. a cheap Explore-style scan routed to a different model) -- but this is architecturally distinct from domain-1's spawn(cli) mechanism (Task tool dispatch is Claude Code's own in-session mechanism, not a headless subprocess spawn), so it needs its own real design pass, not a copy of tsk-62v's shape. High-risk/spike mode expected -- needs fgos-exploring/fgos-planning to actually shape it before any code. Design record: docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md, plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260731-1758-capacity-backend-dispatch-proposal-report.md (design doc's own domain model), plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260801-1159-synthesis-goal-constraints-gaps-report.md section 4.3 (agentic capability vs cheap capability gap, directly relevant to domain-2's own risk).

payload.text: RUL12 fix: sua 1 CHO DUY NHAT -- frontier.mjs:160 RESOLVED_STATUSES tu {done, wontfix} thanh {delivered, retrospective, cleanup, done, wontfix}. Constant nay dung CHUNG boi 6 module (frontier.mjs depsReady + hasOpenDescendant/lineage cha-con, claim-port.mjs, impact.mjs, graph-metrics.mjs, entropy.mjs) -- tat ca deu hoi 'item nay con anh huong CODE/graph khong', va retrospective/cleanup la hanh chinh+hoc tap, khong doi code nua nen nen coi la resolved giong nhau. Can cu: comment goc frontier.mjs tu dinh nghia done (cho muc dich mo-dependent) la '"accepted into the main tree"' -- dung nghia goc ma 'delivered' moi la thu khop chinh xac, 'done' xua nay bi gop 2 nghia (merge xong + dong so hanh chinh xong). fgos rollup (dem k/n done, bao cao) la module KHAC, KHONG dung RESOLVED_STATUSES -- giu nguyen dem done that, khong bat buoc sua cung luc.
payload.rationale: Nguoi xac nhan truc tiep (2026-08-01). Sua 1 constant fix ca 6 consumer cung luc, dung dung y nghia D5 da dinh nghia tu dau -- khong phai workaround.

payload.text: Them dung 2 canh moi vao fsm.mjs de xu ly diem hong 'khong duong thoat khi harness cleanup->done phat hien loi': (1) cleanup -> blocked, doi 'reason' bat buoc -- mirror y het khuon awaiting-approval->blocked da co (cung code path, cung RUL5 pattern). (2) blocked -> delivered, mechanical, KHONG can reason -- mirror y het blocked->awaiting-approval (fan-out-parallel D18, 'reconcile retry, khong phai rejection'). blocked's 3 cua ra co san (->todo, ->doing, ->awaiting-approval) KHONG doi, tu nhien phu case rework that (vd merge bi revert sau delivered, can sua code lai that su). Canh moi (2) rieng phu case retry co hoc nhe (vd retrospective loop crash giua chung, chi can chay lai, khong can sua code).
payload.rationale: 2 case that: (A) merge bi revert tren main sau khi item da delivered (chinh kich ban nguoi dung tu neu lam ly do thiet ke TTL cleanup) -- can quay lai todo/doing sua that, dung cua co san. (B) retrospective loop crash/chua thuc su chay xong (LLM timeout,...) -- chi can retry, di vong qua todo se phi -- can cua rieng blocked->delivered. Khong co canh nao ca thi item ket vinh vien tai cleanup cho case (A) -- fgos move van di dung bang FSM, khong co cua hau admin, mau thuan voi chinh dong luc TTL cleanup nguoi dung neu ra.
payload.alternatives: Option (b) thuan '0 canh moi, cu o nguyen tai cleanup, chi ghi friction' -- bi loai vi khong co duong thoat cho case (A), rui ro ket vinh vien.

patch.title: task-dispatch (in-session Agent/Task tool) capacity-aware routing is a known, unclaimed design gap
patch.description: task-dispatch (in-session Agent/Task tool dispatch, kind: "task" in CAPACITY_KINDS) capacity-aware routing is a known, unclaimed design gap in the agent-executor cluster. tsk-5l2's own scope explicitly deferred it (point 9: originally called 'domain-2', 'a separate item, deliberately out of scope here'), and no backlog item exists for it yet (checked). Today, every in-session subagent spawn (Explore, code-reviewer, cavecrew-*, etc, via the Agent/Task tool) always runs full Claude, unconditionally -- unlike cli-dispatch (headless runner, originally called 'domain-1'), which already routes through capacities.<id> via tsk-62v's mechanism. Applying the same 'cheapest cost for adequate quality' objective to task-dispatch would let a skill declare a capacityId for a specific subagent task (e.g. a cheap Explore-style scan routed to a different model) -- but this is architecturally distinct from cli-dispatch's spawn(cli) mechanism (Task tool dispatch is Claude Code's own in-session mechanism, not a headless subprocess spawn), so it needs its own real design pass, not a copy of tsk-62v's shape. High-risk/spike mode expected -- needs fgos-exploring/fgos-planning to actually shape it before any code. Design record: docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md, plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260731-1758-capacity-backend-dispatch-proposal-report.md (design doc's own model, there still called domain-1/domain-2), plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260801-1159-synthesis-goal-constraints-gaps-report.md section 4.3 (agentic capability vs cheap capability gap, directly relevant to task-dispatch's own risk).

patch.title: Generalize the cli-dispatch-for-cheap-cross-provider-tasks pattern beyond fgos-submit-assist to any
patch.description: task-dispatch (in-session Agent/Task tool) has no path to a non-Claude backend at all -- Claude Code's own Agent/Task tool only selects among Claude models (opus/sonnet/haiku via an agent definition's model field), never an external CLI. So a cross-provider 'cheap capacity' need inside a live session cannot route through the Agent tool by construction; the only real mechanism is shelling out to an external CLI directly -- i.e. reusing cli-dispatch's own resolveCapacityCli/spawn mechanism via Bash, exactly what fgos-submit-assist's own classify step (tsk-5l2) already does once wired. This narrows the gap originally filed here (previously framed as 'task-dispatch needs its own separate architecture, distinct from cli-dispatch') -- it does not: task-dispatch for a Claude-family choice uses the Agent tool (agent definitions' own model field already covers this), task-dispatch for a cross-provider choice reuses cli-dispatch's existing spawn mechanism via Bash, same as fgos-submit-assist already proves works. The real, narrower gap: fgos-submit-assist is the only skill wired this way today -- there is no general, reusable pattern/helper any OTHER skill could follow to declare 'shell out to this capacityId via Bash if configured+present, else fall back to a real Agent/Task subagent spawn' without re-deriving fgos-submit-assist's own wiring from scratch. Scope: extract that pattern (a shared how-to or a small skill-facing helper) so future skills don't rebuild it ad hoc. Design record: docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md, docs/how-to/wire-a-skills-classify-step-through-an-agent-executor-capacity.md (fgos-submit-assist's own real precedent to generalize from).

payload.text: SUA decision #2 (seq 3481): tach RUL58 (acceptance-evidence) khoi RUL50 (retrospective/cleanup xong chua). RUL58 gate o CA 3 cua vao delivered (doing->delivered, awaiting-approval->delivered, blocked->delivered) -- khong con dat o cleanup->done. RUL50-content (gio la dieu kien retrospective+cleanup that su xong) van gate rieng o cleanup->done, khong doi.
payload.rationale: Phat hien khi doi chieu 2 quyet dinh da chot rieng le: RUL12 mo dependent tai delivered (seq 3511) + RUL58 dat o cleanup->done (seq 3481, cu) => dependent co the mo dua tren item CHUA TUNG duoc kiem acceptance-evidence, phai doi toi TTL cleanup xong moi biet co dat tieu chi hay khong -- lo hong that. RUL58 la kiem CHAT LUONG deliverable (dependent PHAI cho), khac RUL50 la quan sat hanh chinh/hoc tap (dependent KHONG can cho, dung y goc tsk-4op). patch.description:
task-dispatch (in-session Agent/Task tool) has no path to a non-Claude backend at all -- Claude Code's own Agent/Task tool only selects among Claude models (opus/sonnet/haiku via an agent definition's model field), never an external CLI. So a cross-provider 'cheap capacity' need inside a live session cannot route through the Agent tool by construction; the only real mechanism is shelling out to an external CLI directly -- i.e. reusing cli-dispatch's own resolveCapacityCli/spawn mechanism via Bash, exactly what fgos-submit-assist's own classify step (tsk-5l2) already does once wired. This narrows the gap originally filed here (previously framed as 'task-dispatch needs its own separate architecture, distinct from cli-dispatch') -- it does not: task-dispatch for a Claude-family choice uses the Agent tool (agent definitions' own model field already covers this), task-dispatch for a cross-provider choice reuses cli-dispatch's existing spawn mechanism via Bash, same as fgos-submit-assist already proves works. The real, narrower gap: fgos-submit-assist is the only skill wired this way today -- there is no general, reusable pattern/helper any OTHER skill could follow to declare 'shell out to this capacityId via Bash if configured+present, else fall back to a real Agent/Task subagent spawn' without re-deriving fgos-submit-assist's own wiring from scratch. Scope: extract that pattern (a shared how-to or a small skill-facing helper) so future skills don't rebuild it ad hoc. Design record: docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md, docs/how-to/wire-a-skills-classify-step-through-an-agent-executor-capacity.md (fgos-submit-assist's own real precedent to generalize from).

cli-dispatch <-> task-dispatch relationship (clarified in-conversation, real and worth pinning): the two are NOT two independent, parallel mechanisms -- they nest, asymmetrically. task-dispatch can always fall through to cli-dispatch (a live session always has Bash, so shelling out to a resolved capacity command is always available -- this is the D1 mechanism above). The reverse is conditional, not structural: cli-dispatch (fgos-runner, a bare Node process, never itself inside a Claude Code session) can never call the Agent/Task tool directly -- but if the specific command it spawns IS 'claude' itself (not a different CLI like agy/gemini), that spawned process is a REAL Claude Code agent loop, and task-dispatch (Task/Agent tool use) becomes available again one level down, inside that worker -- gated entirely by whatever --allowedTools the spawned invocation was given. Today's own committed .fgos-runner.json scopes every executor's --allowedTools narrowly (e.g. 'Bash(git add:*),Bash(git commit:*)' for the default worker) -- deliberately excluding Task/Agent tool access for spawned workers today, a config choice, not a hard technical wall. A CLI other than 'claude' (agy, gemini, ...) can never nest task-dispatch at all, regardless of config -- Task/Agent tool is specific to the Claude Code harness, not a generic capability other CLIs share.

payload.title: Bug: fgos approve's crash-orphan-checkout-reclaim step (used when a leaf item's merge target
payload.description:
Bug: fgos approve's crash-orphan-checkout-reclaim step (used when a leaf item's merge target worktree needs reclaiming) destructively removes a LIVE, in-use worktree — including an ancestor worktree this session was actively working in, plus its nested child worktree — even though the overall approve/merge operation only PARTIALLY succeeded (the git merge itself landed, but the item's own state transition to done then failed with a separate error: "cannot move to done from stage executing — must pass through compound-learn stage first", exit code 2). No data was lost (branches/commits survived in the object database), but the worktree directories vanished from disk mid-operation without warning, breaking the active session's own cwd.

Root cause chain, confirmed by direct investigation during tsk-4iv-1's own merge:
1. Every pick'd worktree gets a certain package directory SYMLINK (not a real directory) pointing at the main checkout's real copy — this symlink pattern is already deliberate/known (see docs/how-to/diagnose-a-verify-fail-post-merge-block-on-approve.md's "genuine gap in the merge machinery" section, tsk-g18/createWorktree fix).
2. .gitignore's ignore pattern for that directory (trailing slash) does NOT match a symlink of the same name, even though it points at a directory — a well-known git gitignore gotcha (gitignore patterns with a trailing slash only match real directories, never symlinks). So every worktree's git status always reports that entry as untracked, permanently.
3. Separately, 6 specific .fgos/* files (coexistence.json, docs/enduser-docs-index.json, entropy-history.jsonl, events.jsonl, events.jsonl.backup-*, gate-bypass.json) are tracked in git history but never materialize on disk in a linked worktree (ADR0020: worktrees never carry their own .fgos/) — so every worktree also always shows these 6 as " D" (deleted) in git status.
4. approve's crash-orphan-checkout-reclaim logic (bin/fgos.mjs, the code path behind the error message "refusing to reclaim checkout of ... it has uncommitted changes, so it is not a genuine crash-orphan") treats ANY non-empty git status --porcelain output (both the untracked symlink AND the 6 phantom-deleted tracked files) as "dirty", refusing to reclaim. This check does NOT share the "same .fgos/ exclusion" that isWorkingTreeClean's scope-aware checks already use elsewhere in this codebase — so it never special-cases the known-structural ADR0020 .fgos/ absence or the known-structural symlink gitignore gap.
5. Once that check is satisfied (worktree looks "clean" after manually restoring the 6 tracked files and removing the stray symlink), the reclaim proceeds to git-merge the child branch AND remove both the child's own worktree and, in my case, the ANCESTOR worktree this whole session was still live in (a session working inside a root item's worktree, which had chained a second EnterWorktree into a child item's worktree per the documented tsk-424 chaining pattern) — with no check for whether that ancestor worktree is still actively in use by the calling session, and no gating on whether the overall approve operation (merge + state transition) will actually fully succeed before performing destructive cleanup.

Impact: any session using the documented tsk-424 pattern (root item worktree -> chained EnterWorktree into a child item's worktree -> approve the child) risks losing its own live working directory out from under it mid-operation. Recovery is possible (branches/commits survive, worktrees can be manually re-added with "git worktree add") but requires understanding this whole chain to diagnose — there is no warning or confirmation before the destructive step.

Suggested areas to fix (not prescribing the exact fix): (a) crash-orphan-checkout-reclaim's cleanliness check should share the same .fgos/ exclusion isWorkingTreeClean already uses, and/or also exclude the known convenience-symlink pattern; (b) the reclaim step should never remove a worktree the CALLING session is still standing inside (or any ancestor of it in a chained-EnterWorktree scenario), regardless of git-status cleanliness; (c) destructive worktree cleanup should not run before the whole approve operation (merge + state transition) is confirmed fully successful — a partial failure should not still trigger full cleanup as if it succeeded.

Discovered live during tsk-4iv-1's merge (2026-08-01). Related but not identical existing items: tsk-2eq (leaf approve holding main-checkout lock on a discarded directory) and tsk-66x (merge list/next false negatives from inside a worktree) — both adjacent to worktree/approve interaction issues but neither describes this specific destructive-reclaim-of-a-live-ancestor-worktree behavior.

payload.title: fgos pick worktree-recreation bug: re-picking an item whose worktree directory already exists (e.g
payload.description: fgos pick worktree-recreation bug: re-picking an item whose worktree directory already exists (e.g. after a prior blocked return, or re-claiming across sessions) can fail with "git worktree add failed for branch ... spawnSync git ENOENT" -- and when it fails, the existing worktree directory has already been silently deleted before the add attempt, leaving the session's cwd pointing at a deleted directory. Branch commits survive (git objects untouched, confirmed via git log on the branch), but the working directory and any session state tied to it is gone. Reproduced twice in one session (tsk-5e97, 2026-08-02): first during a mid-flow re-pick after decompose moved the item to executing (claim auto-released), second during a re-pick after a blocked return. Both times a bare retry of "fgos pick <id>" from the main checkout succeeded and created a NEW worktree path with a different random suffix, reusing the branch (all commits intact) -- so the fix scope is likely in the worktree-add/recreate path inside src/runner/worktree.mjs or wherever fgos pick shells out to "git worktree add", not a data-integrity bug, but a real reliability bug that silently destroys the session's working directory before reporting the failure. Investigate: does pick's recreate-path do a "remove stale worktree entry" step before "git worktree add", and can that removal race with or precede a transient/misresolved git binary lookup (spawnSync ENOENT) in the same call, given this repo runs many concurrent worktree sessions.

payload.title: fgos discover overwrites a locked verify command: resolveDiscovery in src/intake/discovery.mjs
payload.description: fgos discover overwrites a locked verify command: resolveDiscovery in src/intake/discovery.mjs writes verdict.verify from judgeDiscovery's own model guess straight onto work.verify with no check for whether a prior session already set a real, locked verify command there. Concretely: tsk-5e97 (2026-08-02) went through fgos-exploring/fgos-planning/fgos-validating first, and fgos-validating explicitly set item.verify to a real, narrow, already-passing command (node --test test/intake/decompose.test.mjs) and locked it in plan.md's Proof-surface section. Only afterward did the session realize fgos-exploring's own CONTEXT.md lock had never actually been released through the discover verb, so it ran "fgos discover tsk-5e97" -- and that call's own judgeDiscovery verdict carried a DIFFERENT, broader verify guess ("npm test", the whole suite) which resolveDiscovery wrote over the already-locked, already-correct value with no warning. The first "fgos return" then re-ran that broad "npm test" and failed on 2 pre-existing unrelated repo tests, moving the item to blocked -- a false-negative return failure caused entirely by the overwrite, not by the item's actual implementation (64/64 on the correct narrow command). Fix scope is likely in resolveDiscovery/judgeDiscovery's verify-handling in src/intake/discovery.mjs: either never overwrite an existing non-empty/non-placeholder work.verify with the model's own guess, or only fill it when the field is empty/placeholder, mirroring how a locked CONTEXT.md is already treated as a stronger trust signal than a fresh model guess elsewhere in the same file (see readLockedContext's docstring in decompose.mjs, reused by discovery.mjs's own resolveDiscovery per tsk-ozl D2).

payload.description: GitNexus impact() MCP tool gave unreliable blast-radius evidence during tsk-480: impact({target:"appendWorkerLog", direction:"upstream"}) reported impactedCount:0 even though src/runner/loop.mjs:702 and :761 really do call it (confirmed by direct grep); impact({target:"runVerb", direction:"upstream"}) returned "Target 'runVerb' not found" even though async function runVerb(...) is a real top-level exported-from-module function in bin/fgos.mjs that dispatches every CLI verb (including 'approve'). Drop and recreate the FTS index." This means the repo's own impact-analysis capability gate (CLAUDE.md, "present" status) is currently unreliable in practice for at least these symbols/files, even though fgos tool query reports full posture -- sessions following the MUST-run-impact rule get false-negative blast-radius evidence (a real caller reported as having zero callers) without any warning that the evidence is untrustworthy. Fix direction: either repair the corrupted FTS index (the analyze command's own error names the fix -- drop and recreate file_fts), or have the impact-analysis capability gate itself detect and surface index staleness/corruption as a distinct posture (e.g. "present-but-unreliable") instead of leaving "present" indistinguishable from a healthy index.

payload.title: Design and build /fgOS:cleanup-loop: a loop skill that scans fgOS work items at status "cleanup"
payload.description: Design and build /fgOS:cleanup-loop: a loop skill that scans fgOS work items at status "cleanup" and runs the existing `fgos cleanup <id>` verb on the ones actually TTL-ready, closing them to done or reporting blocks, until the pool is empty or a stop condition trips. Mirrors the existing discover-next/discover-loop pair (bare per-id CLI verb + no existing pool-picker), not merge-loop (which already had a CLI-level ranked next). Needs a new pool-picker (e.g. src/state/cleanup-pool.mjs, pickNextCleanupItem) that pre-filters by TTL elapsed (reusing cleanup-harness.mjs's exported checkCleanupTTLElapsed) before ever calling fgos cleanup <id> — calling that verb on a not-yet-TTL-elapsed item currently parks it straight to blocked, which would be wasteful blocked/recovery churn if the loop invoked it blindly on every cleanup-status item. CLI verb/naming for this loop was explicitly left to the implementer in docs/history/work-item-status-delivered-retrospective-cleanup/CONTEXT.md. Scope: new src/state/cleanup-pool.mjs + its test, fgOS:cleanup-next skill (single item, wraps fgos cleanup <id> via the new picker), fgOS:cleanup-loop skill (wraps /loop around /fgOS:cleanup-next, recursing into the built-in loop skill, not ck-loop — same pattern merge-loop/discover-loop already establish and docs/explanation/why-merge-loop-recurses-into-loop-not-ck-loop.md documents). No CLI/FSM changes needed — fgos cleanup <id> and its harness already exist and are reused as-is.

payload.title: fgos pick/take pass repoRoot: process.cwd() instead of deriving from --dir, so a claim-release +
payload.description: fgos pick/take pass repoRoot: process.cwd() instead of deriving from --dir, so a claim-release + re-pick sequence run from inside the very worktree being torn down (bin/fgos.mjs:1715 pick, :1652 take; worktree.mjs:192-229 reclaimOrphanedCheckout, :282-321 createWorktree) spawns 'git worktree add' with cwd pointed at a directory git itself just force-removed, surfacing as 'spawnSync git ENOENT'. Reproduced 2026-08-02 working tsk-2ie: session inside worktree A (fgw/tsk-2ie), engine-driven discover/decompose released the claim, take correctly refused (has own branch, use pick), pick then force-removed worktree A via reclaimOrphanedCheckout while repoRoot==worktree A's own path (its cwd), then failed re-adding it from the now-deleted cwd. tsk-4m0's D1 auto-revert (claim-port.mjs:256-264) already saves the CLAIM (uses dir, unaffected) so retrying from the main checkout works cleanly and no work is lost -- but tsk-4m0 explicitly scoped out fixing the ENOENT trigger itself, only its consequence. Minimal fix: pick/take handlers should derive repoRoot from --dir (e.g. path.dirname(dir)) instead of process.cwd(), so git operations always target the stable main checkout named by --dir, never the caller's possibly-doomed shell cwd; defense in depth, reclaimOrphanedCheckout/createWorktree could also refuse rather than force-remove when orphanPath resolves equal to repoRoot itself.

payload.title: Tôi muốn nâng cấp khâu discover, có vẻ nó hoạt động không có ích gì cả
payload.description:
Tôi muốn nâng cấp khâu discover, có vẻ nó hoạt động không có ích gì cả.

Chúng ta chạy 15 rounds cho các item và đều ra unclear.
Exit 0, unclear, parked. Iteration 4: cleared=0, parked=4, skipped=0.

Tôi muốn discover nó phải hoạt động được như mức của skill '/ck:research'.

Khi chúng ta submit 1 task, discover sẽ giúp:
1. tự làm rõ và phân loại ban đầu về yêu cầu của task (đọc hiểu và tự phát biểu lại cho hoàn chỉnh) có thể update lại task description và title. đây gọi là làm sạch yêu cầu.
2. tìm hiểu các task liên đới đã làm/chưa làm để enrich thông tin, để rõ hơn về scope.
3. dựa vào những gì đã thu thập, xác định cái gì rõ, cái gì chưa rõ.
4. tự lập một plan để đi thu thập thông tin và research thêm về vấn đề mà task đang đặt ra (mà không yêu cầu có sự tham gia của con người). plan nên gồm và không giới hạn (llm có thể đề nghị thêm trước ở đây và cho phép trong quá trình làm việc llm thông minh tự bổ xung)
- scan code liên quan để hiểu thêm và làm rõ
- research online các câu hỏi vấn đề liên quan (tự suy ra các research phrase/keywords để research)

sau khi có được thông tin, lúc này thực sự đánh giá, phân loại xem nó rõ hay không rõ, đầy đủ thông tin hay chưa, có vấn đề gì càn phải có con người quyết định hay mọi thứ đã rõ ràng rồi.
ý ltât cả kết quả thu thập được cần được save lại để sử dụng cho các bước sau.

Các câu hỏi quan tâm khác là chúng ta có thu thập và tạo ra thông tin trong quá trình research, như vậy có tạo worktree không, có gây conflict không?

Hãy distill kỹ các skill của Claudekit (ck) như research, scoute và bộ superpower xem có gì đặc biệt chổ này. nhớ trong cụm này có sử dụng rất nhiều capacity, nên tận dụng cơ chế này của chúng ta để có thể phát huy tính kinh tế và tính điều phối công việc song song.

patch.title: Build /fgOS:retro-loop skill: loop wrapper over status "retrospective", running fgos-compounding
patch.description: Mirror cleanup-loop shape (tsk-dvc) for the retrospective half of the delivered/retrospective/cleanup chain. `fgos retrospective` (D9, tsk-3wo) already sweeps ALL delivered items to retrospective in one mechanical call — no N/T threshold exists or is needed (superseded open question from this items former batch-trigger scope, answered as moot: no daemon auto-triggers, a human/loop always triggers explicitly). What is missing: (1) src/state/retro-pool.mjs — pickNextRetrospectiveItem, filters status==retrospective; (2) fgOS:retro-next skill — single item, invokes fgos-compounding (already retargeted to status retrospective per tsk-1zi) via the new picker, then `fgos move <id> --to cleanup` on success; (3) fgOS:retro-loop skill — wraps the built-in /loop around retro-next, same recursion pattern as merge-loop/discover-loop/cleanup-loop (docs/explanation/why-merge-loop-recurses-into-loop-not-ck-loop.md), stop rules: pool empty, or same item blocked twice in a row. No CLI/FSM changes needed — retrospective sweep and fgos-compounding retarget already exist and are reused as-is.

payload.text: D1 (tsk-3o3): retro-next calls `fgos retrospective` sweep every iteration before picking — one /fgOS:retro-loop invocation drains delivered->retrospective->cleanup end-to-end, no separate manual sweep step needed.
payload.rationale: Verified safety: fgos retrospective (bin/fgos.mjs:948-957) commits one moveWork event per item inside its own loop, so a mid-sweep interruption leaves already-swept items durably at retrospective and unswept items untouched at delivered -- no corruption, no atomic all-or-nothing requirement. 24 items sat at delivered with nothing auto-sweeping them (grep confirmed only bin/fgos.mjs's manual verb calls case 'retrospective'). Matches user's own framing: no daemon, a trigger (the loop itself) does the work.

payload.description:
resolveDiscovery unclear-lại crash khi item đã đang awaiting-human: putInAwaiting cố tự-transition awaiting-human -> awaiting-human, FSM chặn cứng, mất verdict mới

resolveDiscovery (src/intake/discovery.mjs) nhánh unclear gọi putInAwaiting vô điều kiện, không kiểm tra work.status hiện tại. Nếu gọi fgos discover <id> trực tiếp trên 1 item ĐÃ đang ở status awaiting-human (park từ lần discover trước, chưa qua fgos answer) và verdict lần này vẫn unclear, putInAwaiting cố move status awaiting-human -> awaiting-human -- FSM (src/state/fsm.mjs) không có cạnh tự-transition này, transitionWork throw StoreError, toàn bộ lệnh discover chết với exit 2: "transitionWork: no transition from \"awaiting-human\" to \"awaiting-human\" for work". Tái hiện thật (2026-08-02): gọi fgos discover trên 3 item tsk-2rp/tsk-42i/tsk-4op (đều đang awaiting-human từ trước) -- cả 3 crash y hệt lỗi này.

Bình thường discover-loop/discover-next không dính vì pickNextDiscoverItem chỉ chọn item status:todo, không bao giờ tự gọi lại discover trên item đã park sẵn -- nhưng gọi thẳng verb CLI fgos discover <id> thì không có rào chắn này, và đây là use-case hợp lệ (re-check 1 item đã park sau khi có thêm context/code mới, mà chưa cần qua fgos answer trước).

Fix đề xuất: guard putInAwaiting trong resolveDiscovery's nhánh unclear -- chỉ gọi khi work.status hiện tại KHÁC awaiting-human. addDiscovery (ghi verdict mới vào lịch sử) vẫn luôn chạy như hiện tại, không đổi -- chỉ bỏ qua cú move status thừa khi item đã park sẵn rồi. Cần test: gọi resolveDiscovery 2 lần liên tiếp trên cùng 1 item với verdict unclear cả 2 lần (mô phỏng đúng case thật vừa tái hiện) -- lần 2 không được throw, verdict mới vẫn được ghi vào view.discovery[id].

payload.descriptionProposal: Thêm field verifyKind cho work-item để gỡ coding-bias trong goal-check. Hôm nay runGoalCheck (src/runner/goal-check.mjs) luôn spawn item.verify như một lệnh shell thật — domain không phải coding (VD marketing) không có lệnh shell nào trả lời 'khách đã ký duyệt banner chưa', nên return/approve của domain đó không dùng được. Đề xuất tối thiểu (YAGNI, không làm executor framework tổng quát): field verifyKind enum 2 giá trị — shell (mặc định, hành vi coding giữ nguyên 100%) và manual-confirm (goal-check pass dựa trên xác nhận của một người role human, không spawn gì, tái dùng claimRole sẵn có). Tách biệt hoàn toàn khỏi việc tách status/statusCategory (tsk-38t, đụng fsm.mjs) và ưu tiên làm trước vì đây là cái chặn CHỨC NĂNG thật, không chỉ ngữ nghĩa. Phạm vi audit thật (theo re-audit round 12 của report ref) là 9 call site runGoalCheck, KHÔNG phải 4: return branch-source + main-source, approve, catchup x2 (chạy role runner — không có người trong đường này), merge.mjs already-merged + verify-before-commit, loop.mjs startupReap + dispatchClaimedItem. Ngoài ra return có 3 gate xếp chồng (clean-tree, HEAD-advance, verify) — verifyKind chỉ đụng gate thứ 3, nên phải quyết luôn item manual-confirm xử lý 2 gate còn lại thế nào. Risk HIGH vì đụng core trust mechanism ('không tin lời tự báo, luôn tự verify độc lập') dùng chung runner + 2 cửa pull + cổng duyệt PR.

payload.description: Capacity dispatch: simplify kind resolution default branch (Claude-backend + live session -> task, else cli); build missing kind:task adapter. Today capacities.<id>.kind has 'cli' (real cli-spawn adapter) and 'task' (declared in CAPACITY_KINDS, zero working adapter -- resolves through the same command/args spawn path as cli, functionally identical to cli today). Discussion decision: default kind resolution collapses to 2 real branches -- (1) resolved executor.command in CLAUDE_CLI_COMMANDS AND currently running inside a live Claude Code session (top-level or nested worker with Task in allowedTools) -> dispatch via Task/Agent tool instead of spawning 'claude -p' subprocess, so the user can observe the child agent's own terminal pane; (2) non-Claude backend OR no live-session Task access available -> cli spawn, unchanged. No separate explicit-override case needed -- that scenario only ever coincides with cross-provider, already covered by branch 2 and the existing allowCrossProvider/CLAUDE_CLI_COMMANDS gate in resolveExecutorConfig (src/runner/dispatch.mjs). This is a NARROWER, code-level companion to tsk-53h's already-pinned cli-dispatch<->task-dispatch nesting rule (docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md) -- tsk-53h scopes the shared skill-facing helper/pattern; this item scopes the concrete default-kind-resolution logic change in dispatch.mjs plus the missing task-dispatch adapter (EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS has only 'cli-spawn' today -- the deferred rpc/app-server adapter dispatch.mjs:716-719 flags). Open question carried over, not yet resolved: since a Node subprocess (dispatch.mjs) cannot itself invoke the Agent/Task tool -- only the calling LLM session can -- the task-kind adapter can't be a spawn-style adapter; it needs to hand back a signal/instruction for the calling session to act on (mirrors resolveCapacityCli's existing domain-2 pattern: resolve, then the calling session itself executes). Design record continuity: docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md, docs/how-to/wire-a-skills-classify-step-through-an-agent-executor-capacity.md.

patch.description: Capacity dispatch: simplify kind resolution default branch (Claude-backend + live session -> task, else cli); build missing kind:task adapter. Today capacities.<id>.kind has 'cli' (real cli-spawn adapter) and 'task' (declared in CAPACITY_KINDS, zero working adapter -- resolves through the same command/args spawn path as cli, functionally identical to cli today). Discussion decision: default kind resolution collapses to 2 real branches -- (1) resolved executor.command in CLAUDE_CLI_COMMANDS AND currently running inside a live Claude Code session (top-level or nested worker with Task in allowedTools) -> dispatch via Task/Agent tool instead of spawning 'claude -p' subprocess, so the user can observe the child agent's own terminal pane; (2) non-Claude backend OR no live-session Task access available -> cli spawn, unchanged. No separate explicit-override case needed -- that scenario only ever coincides with cross-provider, already covered by branch 2 and the existing allowCrossProvider/CLAUDE_CLI_COMMANDS gate in resolveExecutorConfig (src/runner/dispatch.mjs). This is a NARROWER, code-level companion to tsk-53h's already-pinned cli-dispatch<->task-dispatch nesting rule (docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md) -- tsk-53h scopes the shared skill-facing helper/pattern; this item scopes the concrete default-kind-resolution logic change in dispatch.mjs plus the missing task-dispatch adapter (EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS has only 'cli-spawn' today -- the deferred rpc/app-server adapter dispatch.mjs:716-719 flags). Open question carried over, not yet resolved: since a Node subprocess (dispatch.mjs) cannot itself invoke the Agent/Task tool -- only the calling LLM session can -- the task-kind adapter can't be a spawn-style adapter; it needs to hand back a signal/instruction for the calling session to act on (mirrors resolveCapacityCli's existing task-dispatch pattern: resolve, then the calling session itself executes). Host-access note (confirmed via env inspection): whether a spawned 'claude -p' worker can use Task tool is NOT automatic -- gated per-executor by --allowedTools in .fgos-runner.json. Real example in this repo's own committed .fgos-runner.json: capacities.judge-discovery grants 'Task' in its allowedTools (works); the global default executor and executors.judge do not include 'Task' (cannot); capacities.judge-decompose declares kind:'task' but has no own command/args override so it falls through to executors.judge, which lacks 'Task' in allowedTools -- an existing config inconsistency worth fixing alongside this item. Design record continuity: docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md, docs/how-to/wire-a-skills-classify-step-through-an-agent-executor-capacity.md.

patch.description:
task-dispatch (in-session Agent/Task tool) has no path to a non-Claude backend at all -- Claude Code's own Agent/Task tool only selects among Claude models (opus/sonnet/haiku via an agent definition's model field), never an external CLI. So a cross-provider 'cheap capacity' need inside a live session cannot route through the Agent tool by construction; the only real mechanism is shelling out to an external CLI directly -- i.e. reusing cli-dispatch's own resolveCapacityCli/spawn mechanism via Bash, exactly what fgos-submit-assist's own classify step (tsk-5l2) already does once wired. This narrows the gap originally filed here (previously framed as 'task-dispatch needs its own separate architecture, distinct from cli-dispatch') -- it does not: task-dispatch for a Claude-family choice uses the Agent tool (agent definitions' own model field already covers this), task-dispatch for a cross-provider choice reuses cli-dispatch's existing spawn mechanism via Bash, same as fgos-submit-assist already proves works. The real, narrower gap: fgos-submit-assist is the only skill wired this way today -- there is no general, reusable pattern/helper any OTHER skill could follow to declare 'shell out to this capacityId via Bash if configured+present, else fall back to a real Agent/Task subagent spawn' without re-deriving fgos-submit-assist's own wiring from scratch. Scope: extract that pattern (a shared how-to or a small skill-facing helper) so future skills don't rebuild it ad hoc. Design record: docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md, docs/how-to/wire-a-skills-classify-step-through-an-agent-executor-capacity.md (fgos-submit-assist's own real precedent to generalize from).

cli-dispatch <-> task-dispatch relationship (clarified in-conversation, real and worth pinning): the two are NOT two independent, parallel mechanisms -- they nest, asymmetrically. task-dispatch can always fall through to cli-dispatch (a live session always has Bash, so shelling out to a resolved capacity command is always available -- this is the D1 mechanism above). The reverse is conditional, not structural: cli-dispatch (fgos-runner, a bare Node process, never itself inside a Claude Code session) can never call the Agent/Task tool directly -- but if the specific command it spawns IS 'claude' itself (not a different CLI like agy/gemini), that spawned process is a REAL Claude Code agent loop, and task-dispatch (Task/Agent tool use) becomes available again one level down, inside that worker -- gated entirely by whatever --allowedTools the spawned invocation was given. Today's own committed .fgos-runner.json scopes every executor's --allowedTools narrowly (e.g. 'Bash(git add:*),Bash(git commit:*)' for the default worker) -- deliberately excluding Task/Agent tool access for spawned workers today, a config choice, not a hard technical wall. A CLI other than 'claude' (agy, gemini, ...) can never nest task-dispatch at all, regardless of config -- Task/Agent tool is specific to the Claude Code harness, not a generic capability other CLIs share.

Generalizing the nesting rule beyond Claude (clarified in-conversation, real and worth pinning): the "cli-dispatch spawns a real agent harness, so task-dispatch-like nesting becomes available one level down" property is not Claude-specific by nature -- it's just that Claude Code is the only harness fgOS currently knows to have it (via Task/Agent tool, gated by --allowedTools). agy/codex are already valid, ordinary cli-dispatch spawn targets today (agy is the running submit-assist-classify example; codex is already in KNOWN_ASSISTANT_CLI_NAMES) -- that's their normal role, no special case needed. If either ever ships its own internal subagent/tool-dispatch mechanism (its own equivalent of Task/Agent tool), the same nesting principle would extend to it: that capability would become available one level down inside that spawn, gated by whatever permission/scope equivalent that harness exposes -- the fix would be recognizing it (mirroring how kind:"task" was carved out specifically for Claude's own mechanism in CAPACITY_KINDS), not redesigning the dispatch model. Not a need to build now -- pinned so a future session doesn't have to re-derive whether the nesting rule is Claude-only by accident or by design (it's the latter: Claude-only today because Claude is the only harness with the property, not because the rule itself assumes Claude).

Correction to the nesting framing above (discovered via 'claude --help'): cli-dispatch is not limited to nested one-level Task access via a plain 'claude -p' spawn -- 'claude' CLI has a real '--agent <agent>' flag ('Agent for the current session. Overrides the agent setting.'), letting cli-dispatch spawn 'claude -p --agent <name> ...' directly, running that named agent definition (.claude/agents/<name>.md, tsk-slq's canonical root) headlessly with no Task/Agent tool nesting needed at all. So for a Claude-family agentType capacity specifically, cli-dispatch and task-dispatch now converge on the SAME achievable outcome (right agent definition + right model on the prompt) -- native Task tool (when the calling session already has it) stays the cheaper/observable choice, but exec'ing 'claude --agent <name>' is always a correct, structurally-available fallback, not a degraded one. See tsk-3sw (dependency of this item) for the concrete resolveCapacityCli/resolveExecutorConfig change this enables.

Shared-helper format preference (decided in discussion, tsk-3sw's follow-on): prefer a single shared skill-facing fragment/reference file (e.g. under .claude/skills/_shared/ or equivalent canonical path) that consumer SKILL.md files point to by path, over each skill copy-pasting the branching prose into its own SKILL.md. Reason: N independent copies drift out of sync the next time this pattern's logic changes (DRY) -- a single referenced source doesn't. Sequencing: write this helper against tsk-3sw's finished resolveCapacityCli return shape (uniform {command,args,provider,model} for both cli and task kind, per tsk-3sw's current description) -- not before that lands.

Reinforces tsk-3sw's own 'scope Claude-only now, file multi-provider as separate follow-on' recommendation -- a real per-provider adapter here is a 3-way branch, not a 2-way one, and not yet worth building without a concrete non-Claude agentType consumer.

Sources (user-provided, not independently re-verified beyond the --help spot-check above): https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/subagents, https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands?surface=cli, https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-basic, https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode.

Capacity dispatch: simplify kind resolution default branch (prefer native Task tool when a live session already has it; else spawn claude --agent). Today capacities.<id>.kind has 'cli' (real cli-spawn adapter) and 'task' (declared in CAPACITY_KINDS, zero working differentiation -- resolves through the same command/args spawn path as cli, functionally identical to cli today).

CORRECTION (supersedes earlier wrong claim in this item's history): 'claude -p' CAN run as a specific named agent definition headlessly -- confirmed via 'claude --help': '--agent <agent> Agent for the current session. Overrides the agent setting.' This means a kind:'task' capacity is NOT structurally blocked for cli-dispatch/spawnWorker as earlier claimed. resolveExecutorConfig can build real command/args for an agentType-only capacity too: command:'claude', args including '-p','{prompt}','--agent',<agentType>,'--model','{model}' (plus whatever --allowedTools/--permission-mode the global default template already uses) -- spawned via the EXISTING cli-spawn adapter, no new EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS entry needed, no resolve-time fail-loud for a missing command/args when agentType is present. This works identically for BOTH cli-dispatch (spawnWorker, headless) and task-dispatch (resolveCapacityCli, in-session) -- the earlier 'signal-return instead of command, only for task-dispatch' design is WRONG and retracted.

Revised design (recommended direction, not yet finalized): resolveCapacityCli's return shape does NOT need to be kind-discriminated after all. It can uniformly keep returning {command,args,provider,model} for every capacity, cli or task alike -- for a kind:'task' capacity with no own command/args, resolveExecutorCommand derives command/args from the global default executor template plus an inserted '--agent',<agentType> pair (new code needed: today's fallthrough only reuses executor/executors.<tier> args verbatim, has no notion of inserting an extra flag). The calling skill (task-dispatch consumer, per docs/how-to/wire-a-skills-classify-step-through-an-agent-executor-capacity.md's pattern) then applies its OWN optional optimization: if it already has live Agent/Task tool access AND the capacity's kind is 'task', it MAY call the Task tool natively instead of exec'ing the resolved command (cheaper -- no subprocess startup -- and observable, per the original agent-terminal transparency goal that started this whole discussion) -- but exec'ing the resolved command is always a valid, correct fallback either way, since both paths produce the same semantic outcome (right agent definition + right model on the prompt). This removes almost all the earlier signal-vs-exec branching complexity from resolveCapacityCli itself and pushes the 'use Task natively when cheap' decision to the skill-side optimization layer, where it belongs (the skill already self-knows its own tool manifest).

Validation (static, config-load time, validateCapacityShape): unchanged plan -- 'agentType', when present, must be a non-empty string, same optional-field pattern as 'model'/'allowCrossProvider' today. No kind-based requirement enforced statically (a single capacities.<id> entry's config is validated once but may be resolved via either path across its lifetime). The earlier proposed 'resolve-time fail-loud in cli-dispatch when kind:task has no command/args' is RETRACTED -- no longer needed, since --agent flag always gives cli-dispatch a real way to resolve it.

Still open, not yet resolved:
1. judge-discovery-style capacity that already declares BOTH kind:'task' AND its own explicit command/args (today's real .fgos-runner.json entry) -- when resolved via task-dispatch, does resolveExecutorConfig's existing precedence (capacity's own command/args wins) still apply unchanged? Likely yes (no special-case needed, byCapacity already wins over derived-from-agentType-template) but not yet traced through code.
2. Model precedence between capacity's tier-derived model (modelForTier/capacity.model) and the named agent definition's own pinned model in its .claude/agents/<name>.md frontmatter (tsk-slq) -- '--model {model}' on the CLI flag path would override whatever the agent file pins, same as today's global executor already does; but native Task tool call's own model param vs. the subagent definition's pinned model precedence is a separate, still-untraced question.
3. judge-decompose gap -- FIXED, commit 784bcbc (widened executors.judge's --allowedTools in .fgos/config.json to Task,WebSearch,WebFetch,Read, matching judge-discovery's own override; also fixed 3 live docs still pointing only at the now-legacy .fgos-runner.json instead of .fgos/config.json's runner section, and re-applied the domain-1/domain-2 -> cli-dispatch/task-dispatch rename in dispatch.mjs/its test after a branch switch had reverted it). No longer open, unaffected by this item's own remaining scope.

Design record continuity: docs/explanation/agent-executor-capacity-aware-dispatch.md, docs/how-to/wire-a-skills-classify-step-through-an-agent-executor-capacity.md.

Traced (confirmed via code read, resolveExecutorConfig in src/runner/dispatch.mjs, not speculation): 'const byCapacity = capacity && (capacity.adapter || capacity.command) ? capacity : undefined; const executor = byCapacity ?? perTier ?? cfg.executor;' -- capacity.kind is NEVER read by this precedence chain. It is only read in two OTHER, separate checks, both gated on kind === 'cli': the fgosDir presence-check, and the cross-provider governance check. kind:'task' triggers neither -- zero resolve-time validation exists for task kind today.

This confirms open question 1 (judge-discovery-style precedence): a capacity declaring BOTH kind:'task' AND its own command/args (like judge-discovery today) always resolves to that own command/args via byCapacity, unconditionally, identically for cli-dispatch and task-dispatch -- both call the exact same resolveExecutorConfig function, no path-based branching exists inside it at all (fgosDir presence/absence only toggles the kind:'cli' presence-check, nothing else).

This also PROVES the risk tsk-3sw already flagged about the planned agentType field: byCapacity's condition checks ONLY 'capacity.adapter || capacity.command' -- it has NO clause for 'capacity.agentType'. So an agentType-only capacity (kind:'task', no command/args, per this item's planned design) would compute byCapacity = undefined today and silently fall through to perTier/global executor, dropping agentType entirely with no error. Concrete required code change (not yet implemented): the byCapacity condition must become 'capacity.adapter || capacity.command || capacity.agentType', with a new branch that derives command:'claude' + args including '--agent', capacity.agentType (built from the global default executor's own args template, per this item's earlier '--agent flag' correction) when only agentType is present.

Model precedence (open question 2) -- RESOLVED empirically, real evidence, not speculation: ran 'claude -p --agent code-simplifier --model haiku --debug-file <log> "say hi"' and grepped the debug log's real dispatched API model field. With '--model haiku' present: log shows 'dispatching to firstParty model=claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' -- the explicit --model flag WINS over code-simplifier's own pinned 'model: opus' frontmatter. Re-ran with '--agent code-simplifier' alone, no --model flag: log shows 'dispatching to firstParty model=claude-opus-5' -- confirms the agent definition's own pinned model is the fallback default when --model is omitted. (Also confirmed separately, before this: '--agent code-simplifier' genuinely loads the right persona -- asked it to quote its own system prompt, got back the real code-simplifier.md persona text and matching tool list, so --agent resolution itself works as expected.)

Confirmed precedence chain: explicit '--model' CLI flag > agent definition's own pinned 'model:' frontmatter (used only when --model is omitted from args).

Resulting open design decision (not yet resolved, this is now a real choice, not an unknown): when building args for an agentType-only capacity (this item's planned '--agent' flag support), should the args template unconditionally include '--model {model}' (from tier/capacity.model, like today's global default executor template always does) -- meaning the capacity's own configured tier always overrides whatever model the named agent definition pins for itself? Or should it OMIT '--model' for agentType capacities, letting the agent definition's own pinned model win, since presumably whoever authored that agent definition (e.g. code-simplifier pinning opus) already made a deliberate model choice for that persona that a work item's generic tier shouldn't silently override? Needs a decision before implementation, not an assumption either way.

IMPORTANT constraint discovered, must shape this item's implementation (see tsk-53h for full evidence, verified live): the planned 'agentType' capacity field must NOT be built Claude-only. 'agy' (already a real cli-dispatch target in this repo, submit-assist-classify) has its OWN independent '--agent <name>' persona-dispatch mechanism + its own 'agent.md' custom-agent file format (different frontmatter schema than Claude's '.claude/agents/<name>.md' -- agy: mainAgent/subagent/hidden/inheritMcp/commandExecutionPolicy/model; Claude: name/description/model/tools). Both CLIs happen to share the flag NAMES '--agent'/'--model' (coincidental, not a shared schema). Verified live: 'agy --model gemini-3.6-flash-high --agent default -p ...' works today.

Design consequence for this item: resolveExecutorConfig's planned args-building for an agentType-only capacity (this item's earlier '--agent flag' correction) cannot assume the executor.command is always 'claude' -- it must build the '--agent'/agent-definition-lookup step per the RESOLVED executor.command (claude vs agy vs any future provider with its own equivalent), or explicitly scope this item to Claude-only for now and file the agy/multi-provider generalization as separate follow-on scope (tsk-slq's canonical agents/<name>.yaml -> per-provider adapter projection idea, tracked in tsk-53h). Needs an explicit scope decision before implementation: build Claude-only now (simpler, matches today's only real agentType precedent, judge-discovery) and file agy-adapter support as future work, OR design the per-provider mapping now. Leaning Claude-only-now per YAGNI (no concrete agy-agentType consumer exists yet, unlike judge-discovery's real Claude case) -- but flagging explicitly rather than silently assuming, since it changes resolveExecutorConfig's shape (single hardcoded '--agent' flag literal vs a provider-keyed lookup).

Host-access detection for task-dispatch resolve (discussed, empirically checked, not yet acted on in code): live env inspection in an actual Claude Code session ('env | grep -iE claude') confirms 'CLAUDECODE' (and CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT/CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID/etc.) really is set by the claude CLI binary itself on startup -- but no env var exposes the session's own allowedTools/permission list (checked: 'env | grep -iE TOOL|ALLOWED|PERMISSION' empty), so no env-based signal can tell task-dispatch's resolve step whether Task/Agent tool is ACTUALLY usable right now, only whether SOME Claude Code process is running at all. Conclusion reached: no code-level host-type detection module is needed. For task-dispatch (resolveCapacityCli, run via the calling skill's own Bash tool call): the calling LLM session already inherently knows its own tool manifest (whether it has Agent/Task tool) with zero code -- self-awareness, not env-var detection -- this is exactly the 'skill-side optimization layer' decision already recorded above (native Task vs exec the resolved command). CLAUDECODE's only remaining use is as a cheap guard: absent means the resolve call is happening OUTSIDE any Claude Code process at all (a plain terminal, cron, non-Claude harness) -- there, even suggesting 'you could use Task' is nonsensical, so resolution should never even hint at kind:'task' semantics in that case, always resolve straight to cli-equivalent args. Not yet wired into any actual code -- a design conclusion to apply during this item's implementation, not a separate open question.

payload.description: bug: main-checkout-lock TOCTOU race gây lock-ambiguous giả (fgos pick/take). tryAcquireOnce() (src/runner/main-checkout-lock.mjs:135-218) tạo lock qua 2 bước tách rời — fs.openSync(lockPath,'wx') rồi fs.writeSync(fd,...) riêng (dòng 137-142); nhánh self-recognition refresh (dòng 165) cũng ghi non-atomic bằng fs.writeFileSync truncate-in-place thay vì write-then-rename. Một reader (claimWork) đọc đúng lúc giữa open và write sẽ thấy file rỗng/nội dung dở dang, parseLockContent() trả null, và acquireMainCheckoutLock fail-closed thành AMBIGUOUS dù không có writer nào thực sự xung đột. Quan sát thực tế: /fgOS:pick tsk-3lx chạy 2026-08-03 08:37:42, ~91s sau commit tự động chore(fgos): sync event log state lúc 08:36:11 (pre-commit hook gọi cùng acquireMainCheckoutLock, ttlMs=DEFAULT_TTL_MS=3min) — trong cửa sổ TTL nên đáng lẽ phải trả HELD, nhưng lỗi thực nhận là claimWork: main checkout lock state ambiguous KHÔNG có lockAgeMs suffix, khớp đúng nhánh unparseable content (dòng 157-158, không carry lockAgeMs) chứ không phải nhánh thiếu-ttlMs (dòng 183, có carry lockAgeMs).
